en.title: Crown Him with Many Crowns
en.author: Matthew Bridges and Godfrey Thring
stanzas:
[D]Crown Him with [Bm]many [G]crowns,
The [D]Lamb up[A7]on His [D]throne.
[D]Hark! How the [A]heav'nly [Bm]anthem [E7]drowns
[A]All music [E7]but its [A]own!
A[D]wake, my [A7]soul, and [D]sing
Of [G]Him who [B7]died for [E7]thee;
And [D]hail Him [G]as thy [A]matchless [D]king
Through [G]all e[D]ter[A7]ni[D]ty!

Crown Him the Lord of life,
Who triumphed o'er the grave,
And rose victorious in the strife
For those He came to save.
His glories now we sing,
Who died, and rose on high,
Who died eternal life to bring,
And lives that death may die.

Crown Him the Lord of love!
Behold His hands and side,
Those wounds, yet visible above,
In beauty glorified:
No angel in the sky
Can fully bear that sight,
But downward bends his burning eye
At mysteries so bright!

Crown Him the Lord of peace!
Whose power a scepter sways
From pole to pole, that wars may cease,
Absorbed in prayer and praise:
His reign shall know no end,
And round His piercèd feet
Fair flowers of paradise extend
Their fragrance ever sweet.

Crown Him the Lord of years,
The Potentate of time,
Creator of the rolling spheres,
Ineffably sublime.
All hail, Redeemer, hail!
For Thou hast died for me;
Thy praise and glory shall not fail
Throughout eternity.

notes: Hymnary warns that "almost no two hymnals include the exact same arrangement" of this text. The Cyber Hymnal prints nine stanzas (Bridges 1-6, Thring 7-9); the five shipped here are the commonly-printed set, in the order most modern hymnals use -- many crowns / life / love / peace / years. Wording is the Cyber Hymnal's, with one correction: it reads "For Thou has died for me", an obvious slip for "hast", which is what Trinity and Timeless Truths print. "piercèd" and its grave accent are the source's. Variant readings to be aware of in stanza 3: Trinity and Timeless Truths have "Rich wounds, yet visible above" and "downward bends his wond'ring eye" where the Cyber Hymnal has "Those wounds" / "burning eye". Key D confirmed by the hymnchords.net chart and Timeless Truths; hymnary's incipit database lists DIADEMATA in E-flat, one semitone away. CHORDS ARE BEST-EFFORT: the published chart is dense (often a chord per syllable, with a real modulation to the dominant across lines 3-4) and its PDF text layout could not be aligned to syllables with confidence, so this chart keeps its harmonic shape but thins it to roughly two changes a bar. VERIFIED 2026-08-02: cross-checked against hymnal.net #142, which agrees on stanzas 1 and 5 apart from printing "matchless King" where the Cyber Hymnal (followed here) has lowercase "king", and shows the usual arrangement drift elsewhere ("And all be prayer and praise", "Fair flowers of glory now extend", "Thy praise shall never, never fail").
